ny_barkeater_cliff_the.blurb: A small trad cliff in the Keene area of the Adirondacks, tucked behind Pitchoff Mountain and looking across toward the Sentinel Range. Twenty-two routes, nearly all protected by your own gear, run from easy fifth-class cracks through the 5.7 to 5.9 range, with a handful of 5.10s and one 5.11 at the top end. It is a friendly place for newer leaders: the lines are short, the cracks are clean and the protection is generally good, so a single rope handles climbing and rappelling. Expect a woodland walk of roughly a mile on a ski trail followed by a short uphill push.

ny_ark_wall.blurb: A roughly 70-foot cliff on the Lake George side of the Adirondacks, a little uphill from the Shelving Rock crags and quieter than they are. Most of its 21 routes are bolted, with a few trad lines mixed in. Grades start around 5.5 and reach into the 5.11s, but the bulk of the climbing sits between 5.7 and 5.10. Because it is partly shaded it suits warm days, and the walk in is short. The cliff was developed fairly recently, so some rock is loose and broken in places and a helmet is wise.
ny_ark_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the hiking lot for Shelving Rock Mountain (also called lot 4), just before the lot used for the Shelving Rock crags.
ny_ark_wall.approach: Follow the hiking trail for about two minutes, then peel off onto a cairned climbers' path that leads to the cliff; allow about 15 minutes to the right-hand side of the wall.

ny_6_the_tower_wall.blurb: The most prominent cliff in the Powerlinez climbing area of Harriman State Park, standing behind a transmission pylon at the edge of the trees. Its 21 routes are mainly trad, with a few set up as top-ropes, running from easy fourth-class and low fifth-class lines up to some stiff 5.11s; the largest group sits around 5.7 to 5.9. The rock is gritty and sharp, with the odd loose section, and the tops are rounded and sloping. Lines are close together, which makes it a handy spot to practise gear placements and take plenty of laps.

ny_westside_outcrops.blurb: A compact urban boulder in Manhattan's Central Park, sitting on the median beside Central Park West near 103rd Street. It holds about twenty problems, mostly easy: the street-facing side is largely V0 and V1 while the shorter end face carries the harder lines, up through the V4 to V7 range. Heights are small, and you will climb in full view of passers-by. Subway and bus stops are close, so it works as a quick session between other plans rather than a destination trip.

ny_b_workout_wall.blurb: The far end of the Near Trapps cliff in the Shawangunks, a short stroll along the base trail beyond the Gelsa area. This is the Gunks' hard-climbing wall: half of its twenty trad lines are 5.12, with a good number of 5.10 and 5.11 routes and a few easier ones to warm up on, so it rewards fit leaders who place gear quickly. A few lines are also set up as top-ropes. Expect sandstone with the horizontal breaks and roofs the Gunks are known for.

ny_stony_clove_west_side.blurb: A winter ice area in the Catskills beside the Stony Clove notch, on the Hunter Mountain side of the highway. Most of the twenty routes are single-pitch water ice, spread from about WI2 up to a single WI5, with the bulk at WI3 and WI4. A couple of mixed lines and a few two-pitch options add variety. The corner lines see only a short spell of morning sun, so they hold their ice well, while the walk in crosses talus under snow and ends along a dark road, so bring a headlamp.
